claims.text: Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitates can be introduced into tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
A controlled alloying and thermal-processing step will produce coherent nanoprecipitates within the RHEA matrix.
SCCPs will improve the radiation tolerance of tungsten-based RHEAs.
SCCPs will preserve the mechanical integrity of tungsten-based RHEAs.
The unmodified baseline is a homogeneous tungsten-based RHEA optimized for high strength and ductility but lacking integrated nanoprecipitates.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as efficient sinks for irradiation-induced vacancies and interstitials.
Defect-sink activity from SCCPs will reduce irradiation-induced defect accumulation, including helium-bubble formation.
Coherent SCCP interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent SCCP interfaces relieve stress concentrations that could otherwise initiate premature cracks.
The beneficial radiation response will hold under high-helium-flux, elevated-temperature conditions representative of plasma-facing components.
Under identical irradiation conditions, the SCCP-modified alloy will have lower irradiation-induced defect density than the unmodified baseline.
Under identical irradiation conditions, the SCCP-modified alloy will exhibit less radiation-induced hardening than the unmodified baseline.
The SCCP-modified alloy will avoid a significant loss of ductility after irradiation.
Tungsten-based RHEAs without SCCPs are known to accumulate irradiation defects that cause mechanical embrittlement over time.
The proposed benefit depends on the nanoprecipitates being uniformly dispersed, coherent with the matrix, and stable during high-temperature irradiation.
Incoherent or compositionally enriched interfacial phases may fail to provide the desired radiation and mechanical improvements.
TEM, nanoindentation, and tensile testing can compare defect populations, hardening, strength, and ductility in irradiated SCCP and control samples.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in defect density and mechanical degradation relative to the control would falsify the hypothesis.
